# trafficserver / fuzz_rec_http

trafficserver's own fuzz target `fuzz_rec_http` ([source](source/fuzz_rec_http.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over trafficserver (apache/trafficserver at 97d2831f).

Copies the input (Size from 8 to 1024 bytes) into a string and, after ts_session_protocol_well_known_name_indices_init registers the well-known protocol names, converts it, read as a comma-separated list of ALPN protocol names, to ALPN wire format with convert_alpn_to_wire_format into a 30-byte (MAX_ALPN_STRING) buffer, and drops the result and the buffer. Before those calls it installs a new Diags object with DiagsPtr::set, and it deletes that object after. It returns -1 for an input with Size below 8 or above 1024.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against trafficserver at commit 97d2831f with 3 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/fuzz_rec_http.cc is trafficserver 97d2831f's tests/fuzzing/fuzz_rec_http.cc with one Theorem Labs change: its length check returns -1, not 1, for an input outside its limits (libFuzzer rejects the input; the driver exits 0, not 78).

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.
